survivors.claim: The conjunction gate checks the status record BEFORE the file, so a host whose docs/design/catalog.md was generated successfully (record present, exit 0) and later deleted by hand never gets it regenerated on any later DESIGN_BRIEF print, and the doctor check (D5, existence-guarded) never runs for it either — the step keeps printing `catalog: N components` from a record whose file is gone. D5 names the file's absence as the trigger; the prior iteration's prescribed fix (run when absent AND no record) is what was implemented, and AC-9's second-run no-re-run pin makes the ordering defensible, so this is advisory only: a cheap tightening is to key the no-retry half on `catalog.exit !== 0` (retry-suppression only for failures), letting a deleted-after-success file regenerate.
survivors.impact: If someone deletes the generated catalog file after a successful run, the driver keeps reporting counts for a file that no longer exists and never rebuilds it.
survivors.evidence: Lines 689–690: `if (status.designStage && status.designStage.catalog) return` then `if (fs.existsSync(catalogMdPath())) return` — the record check short-circuits before the file check. Spec D5 (line 41): "runs D4 at `DESIGN_BRIEF`'s print when `docs/design/catalog.md` is absent". Not executed as a repro (advisory, no spec-side contradiction quotable against the prescribed conjunction fix from reviewer-return-2 s0).
